ideas.idea: Let a city guide name markets that are missing from the dataset (or show 'recently closed' on a market card), so pages like Columbus with stale USDA data still show the real lineup.
Thin cities (2 markets) lean on nearby-town markets in the guide. A template slot for 'Nearby towns' tips (Emmaus, Easton) with distance would make it clear these are outside city limits.
Raleigh's biggest draw is one daily state-run market with restaurants and a garden center. A 'What's inside' block for market halls (shops, restaurants with hours) would beat cramming them into tips.
San Diego has a fishermen's market (Tuna Harbor Dockside) that is not a produce market. A 'Seafood market' tag or badge on market cards would help visitors find it, like night or winter markets.

Madison's main market changes venue by season (Capitol Square, Monona Terrace, Garver Feed Mill). A 'Where is it this week' block driven by dated venue ranges would answer the top off-season question better than tips.
Hunter's Creek is a monthly market (third Sunday). Market cards could show 'Monthly' with the next date when a market publishes a date list, so visitors don't expect it every week.

Ann Arbor's main market changes days by season (Wed and Sat May-Dec, Sat only Jan-Apr). A seasonal schedule line on the market card ('Now: Sat 8am-3pm') would answer the off-season question without a tip. Also worth a periodic check that listed websites still belong to the market (Cobblestone's domain was taken over).
